blockingFindings: In scripts/codex/launch.mjs, the successful-review close handler calls comparisonBaseSha() outside a try/catch. If canonical base resolution fails or changes during review, the async callback can reject before emitting review-binding-changed and a terminal failed event, violating fail-closed terminal coverage.
nonBlockingRisks: A persistence-finalization failure after terminal success can leave a successful trace without a published shell review result; Codex-app recovery is covered, but shell recovery is not explicitly proven.
missingNegativeTests: Simulate comparisonBaseSha throwing during successful-child close and verify exactly one failed terminal event, no review-result persistence, and nonzero exit.

architectureAssessment.deepModules: Review parsing, cancellation, binding, and publication are separated into focused helpers, though launch.mjs remains a broad orchestration module.
architectureAssessment.hexagonalArchitecture: Codex execution remains isolated behind the child-process adapter, with review binding and persistence kept within the governed local boundary.
architectureAssessment.eventedBoundaries: Structured redacted progress events are present, but the canonical-base exception path can bypass the terminal event boundary.

exactNextAction: Guard close-handler revision revalidation with fail-closed error handling, add the canonical-base failure regression test, rerun required checks, and submit a fresh review head.
